resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives a 50-foot steel tower for 1948; the 1948 state report and the 1949 newspaper both give 54 feet, and the register gives 54 feet 6 inches for the same steel tower at Baughman. The record keeps 16.5 m (54 feet).
Newspaper reports from September 1933 disagree, giving 14 by 14 in one and 10 by 10 in another. The 1948 report later describes a 14 x 14 cabin on the steel tower.

resolved_conflicts.field: current use of the Baughman tower
resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register entry, with no date given, calls the lookout in active service; an April 2026 visit report lists it as not staffed and says staffing stopped in the early 2000s. Not resolved; the story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Relocated tower: story covers both the Shivigny site (gone, no current description) and the Baughman lookout where the steel tower now stands. Baughman naming is disputed (cherylhill says no such geographic name; story says the Baughman lookout). Legal location conflict: Oregon Lookouts header 26S-2W-34 vs its 1948 report T34S R2W sec 27; not used. Agency set from firelookout.com listing (Umpqua National Forest); the 1949 article says the tower was erected by the Douglas Forest Protective Association and manned by Forest Service lookouts. Brief had no agency. Brief's coordinates 43.27041,-122.92043 come from the FFLA directory and are not checked against a page. Weebly newspaper excerpts are secondary transcriptions. Access left unset; no source gives current access to the Shivigny site. The Baughman page on cherylhill.net says reaching that lookout requires a Coos Bay–Millicoma district recreation permit. A 1939 newspaper mention of a lookout on Shivney butte is omitted as not clearly this site.
